chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'One buys sheep, or a group buys sheep, then they are brought into a house, then a man stands at the door and counts one, two, three, four, five, then he draws the lot.' He said: 'This is not valid; the lots are only valid if the distribution is equal/fair.'

key_terms.السِّهَامُ: The lots or arrows used for drawing lots
key_terms.الْقِسْمَةُ: The division or distribution of shares

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of drawing lots (qur'ah) in dividing goods or livestock in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the validity of drawing lots (*qur'ah*) for dividing livestock is contingent upon the fairness and equality of the shares (*al-qismah*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that chance-based distribution is only permissible when it ensures equitable outcomes, preventing exploitation in communal property division. The condition of 'equality' here refers to the substantive fairness of the division rather than mere procedural correctness.
